answer: LINE combines first-order proximity with textual features when a new vertex arrives with no learned embedding from the graph structure, so its representation must be inferred from its text content and the existing first-order proximity information in the network. In other words, this is used in the inductive/new-node setting, especially for vertices that are newly added and may be sparsely connected or not yet well represented by edges.
confidence_reasoning: This is a well-known use of LINE in inductive settings for new or cold-start vertices, but the exact phrasing can vary across papers and implementations.
